canDo: Hold a passport application through its entire declared lifecycle on one object — Passport_Application__c — with twelve Status__c values from Draft to Delivered, six record types (Fresh, Re-issue, Tatkal, Lost/Damaged, Minor, Diplomatic/Official) and a Path that renders the stage bar on the record page.

Save a half-finished form. Drafts are deliberately saveable with almost nothing filled in; the four validation rules only bite once Status__c leaves Draft, which is the whole point of the "a draft is the same object in Draft status" design.

Carry a golden identity record separate from the application. Citizen__c is the current truth about a person; the application keeps its own as-submitted copy of the applicant's details (see the Data Model section for why that duplication is intentional).

Model the fulfilment tail end to end in metadata: Passport__c (the issued booklet, with its own Ordinary / Diplomatic / Official record types), Print_Job__c and Dispatch__c — with booklet pages, validity, ECR, category, place of issue and the delivery address all derived by cross-object formula rather than re-keyed.

Price an application without code. Fee_Matrix__mdt carries a record per record-type × booklet-pages × validity combination, and SLA_Config__mdt carries a normal and a Tatkal target for every processing stage.

Enforce role- and criteria-based visibility. A role hierarchy, public groups, work queues and criteria-based sharing rules route Tatkal, high-risk, diplomatic, granting-stage and fulfilment-stage records to the right teams without opening the org up.

Present a purpose-built app. The Application Management Console has a branded navy header, a curated tab set, a custom Lightning home page and four LWCs (home dashboard, application sidebar, sidebar summary, risk meter) backed by Apex controllers with test classes.

Reuse picklist vocabulary. Shared value sets — Indian states, gender, region, payment mode/status, document status, fulfilment status, courier partner, relationship, severity, language — are Global Value Sets, so a new object inherits the vocabulary instead of re-declaring it.
cannotDo: No approval anywhere. Granting a Diplomatic or Official passport is currently a picklist change by anyone with edit access — there is no Approval Process in the org at all.

No citizen self-service. There is no Experience Cloud site for applicants; every step of the journey is staff-mediated. The inherited Internal Zone community and its self-registration controllers are template leftovers, not a PSK applicant portal.
No reporting. Zero reports, dashboards or custom report types exist for any PSK object, so there is no way to answer "how many applications are stuck at Police Verification" other than a list view.

No region-based sharing. Enterprise Territory Management is not enabled and cannot be enabled by deploy, and criteria-based sharing cannot read PSK_Office__r.Region__c through the lookup — so office/region scoping is unimplemented.
No field-level encryption. Shield Platform Encryption is unavailable in Developer Edition, so Aadhaar_Token__c is stored as plain text.
No integrations. n8n, Twilio and the AI enrichment layer are designed for but not built; Notification_Log__c exists and is empty of real sends.

No visa department. Visa_Application__c, Country__c and Sponsor__c are unbuilt, although a Visa Processing Team role, a PSK Visa Team public group and a PSK_Visa_Type global value set are already in place waiting for them.
No localisation. Every objectTranslations/ bundle is an en_US stub echoing the English label, despite Citizen__c.Preferred_Language__c existing to record a citizen's language preference.

erd.calloutTitle: Why the application duplicates the applicant's details
calloutBody: Passport_Application__c carries its own First_Name__c, Last_Name__c, Date_of_Birth__c, Mobile__c and full address even though it also has a Citizen__c lookup to the golden identity record. That is deliberate, not an oversight.

A passport application is a legal instrument. The details as declared at submission are what get printed into the booklet, what the police verify against, and what an audit or a court would later be asked to examine. They are a snapshot of a declaration made on a date, not a live view of a person.

If those fields were cross-object formulas reading Citizen__r, then the day a citizen moved house or corrected a spelling, every historical application would silently rewrite itself — including applications already granted and printed. The record of what was declared would be destroyed by the act of keeping the citizen record current. Snapshotting is the only correct answer.
Citizen__c therefore answers "who is this person now"; the application answers "what did they declare then". Both are needed, and they are allowed to disagree.
avoidedBody: Passport__c re-keys nothing from the application. Booklet_Pages__c, Validity_Years__c, ECR_Status__c and Passport_Category__c are TEXT(Application__r.…) formulas, Holder_Name__c is assembled by formula from the application's name parts, and Place_of_Issue__c is PSK_Office__r.Name. The booklet's own facts — file number, issue and expiry dates, status — are the only stored fields.
Dispatch__c builds Delivery_Address__c as a formula over Passport_Application__r's address lines, so a courier label can never drift from the application it was raised against.

Family_Member__c reads Member_Date_of_Birth__c and Member_Mobile__c through Related_Citizen__r, and Display_Name__c falls back to a typed Member_Name__c only when there is no linked citizen record to read from.
Print_Job__c and Dispatch__c both expose ARN__c as Passport_Application__r.Name rather than storing the ARN string.
The rule of thumb the model follows: snapshot a declaration, derive a fact.

lifecycle.intro: This is the single most important test in the pack. It exercises every validation rule, every stage-entry stamp, and the automation that spawns the fulfilment records. Run it end to end in one sitting and note the ARN so the trail can be re-read afterwards.
preconditions: At least one active PSK__c office record exists (needed for Place_of_Issue__c to resolve on the eventual passport).
The running user has PSK_App_Access — or, for a persona pass, the relevant PSK_* persona permission set.
Note the current record counts for Passport__c, Print_Job__c and Dispatch__c before you start, so you can prove the deltas.

steps.action: New Passport Application from the tab; pick record type Fresh. Save with only First Name filled in.
steps.expect: Saves. Status defaults to Draft. Is_Draft__c is true. Path shows Draft as the current step with its guidance text.

steps.action: Set Status = Submitted while Last Name / DOB / Mobile / Address Line 1 are still blank.
steps.expect: Blocked by Require_Core_Fields_On_Submit: "First Name, Last Name, Date of Birth, Mobile and Address Line 1 are required before submitting."

steps.action: Fill Last Name, Date of Birth, Mobile, Address Line 1, State and Pincode. Link a Citizen__c and a PSK_Office__c. Set Status = Submitted.
steps.expect: Saves. Submitted_Date__c and Stage_Entered_Date__c are stamped. Fee is populated from Fee_Matrix__mdt for Fresh × booklet pages × validity.
Saves. Stage_Entered_Date__c re-stamps. Payment_Status__c is Not Paid or Pending.

steps.action: Create a Payment__c child for the full Fee__c with Status = Success, then advance.
steps.expect: Saves. Payment_Status__c becomes Paid and Payment_Date__c is set. The Payments related list shows the child.

steps.action: Advance. Work the Document_Checklist_Item__c children to Received / Verified.
steps.expect: Saves. Checklist items appear in their related list. Documents_Verified__c can be ticked once all items verify.

steps.action: Advance. Confirm a Police_Verification__c child exists with PV_Type__c matching the record type's allowed values (Fresh permits Pre-PV / Post-PV only).
steps.expect: Saves. PV record reachable from the Police Verifications related list. Setting its Status to Adverse should make the record visible to PSK Managers via the Adverse To Managers sharing rule.

steps.action: On a separate application whose Payment_Status__c is not Paid, set Status = Granting.
steps.expect: Blocked by Cannot_Grant_With_Pending_Payment: "Payment must be Paid before the application can move to Granting."

steps.action: On the main application, advance to Granting.
steps.expect: Saves — payment is Paid. Granted_Date__c is stamped. Granting Officers gain Edit via the Granting Stage To Granting Officers sharing rule.

A Passport__c record is created and linked back via Application__c. Its Booklet_Pages__c, Validity_Years__c, ECR_Status__c, Passport_Category__c and Holder_Name__c formulas resolve from the application; Place_of_Issue__c resolves to the PSK office name. A Print_Job__c is created with Status__c queued and Queued_Date__c stamped.

steps.action: Mark the print job printed with Quality_Check_Passed__c = true, then advance the application.
steps.expect: Print_Job__c.Turnaround_Hours__c computes. A Dispatch__c is created with a courier partner, a tracking number, an expected delivery date, and Delivery_Address__c resolved by formula from the application address.

steps.action: Set the dispatch Delivered_Date__c and Received_By__c, then advance the application to Delivered.
steps.expect: Saves. Dispatch__c.Transit_Days__c computes. Passport__c.Status__c is Active and Days_To_Expiry__c is positive.
Blocked by No_Backward_Move_Once_Delivered: "A Delivered application cannot be moved back to an earlier stage."

finalAssertions: Exactly one Passport__c, one Print_Job__c and one Dispatch__c exist for the ARN — no duplicates from re-saving a stage.
No validation rule fired at a stage where it should have been silent (in particular, nothing blocked the Draft save).
No validation rule was bypassed: re-run the two negative steps and confirm they still block after the record reached Delivered.
Field history on the application shows one Status__c transition per advance and no unexplained edits.
A Notification_Log__c row exists for each stage that is meant to notify, and none exists where Notification_Consent__c is false.

personaMatrix.intro: Personas are expressed as permission sets over a Private org-wide default, layered on a role hierarchy for vertical visibility and criteria-based sharing rules for lateral visibility. The persona set list below is enumerated from force-app/main/default/permissionsets/PSK_* at generation time — if a set is missing from the table it has not landed in the tree yet.
verifyHow: Assign one persona set at a time to the spare Salesforce Platform user, then open the Application Management Console as that user (see the licence note in Org Limits for why a single user is reused).

For each object in the row: attempt Read (open a record from the tab), Create (New from the tab), Edit (change a field), Delete (the Delete action). Record what actually happened, not what the set claims.
Cross-check with Setup → Users → the test user → View Summary (object and field permissions) and with the record-level Sharing button on a sample record.

For PII fields — Date_of_Birth__c, Aadhaar_Token__c, Aadhaar_Verified__c, Mobile__c — verify field-level security separately from object access. A persona that can open the record must not automatically be able to read the Aadhaar token.
Verify queue visibility: each of the work queues should list only the records the persona is meant to work.

expectedPersonas.label: Front-line Officer / Data Entry
expectedPersonas.shape: Create and edit applications in Draft/Submitted, manage citizens, family members, appointments and slots. No granting, no fulfilment, no risk review. This is the widest-blast-radius set — check its field-level security on Aadhaar_Token__c and Date_of_Birth__c carefully.

expectedPersonas.label: Verification Officer (documents + police)
expectedPersonas.shape: Read applications; full control of Document Checklist Items, Objections and Police Verification records. Should not be able to move Status past Police Verification. Reads high-risk applications through High Risk To Verification.

expectedPersonas.label: Granting Officer
expectedPersonas.shape: Edit applications at Granting/Printing and create Passport records. Must NOT be able to edit the applicant declaration fields — that is the snapshot, and a granting officer rewriting it would defeat the whole point of §2.1 of PSK.md.

expectedPersonas.label: Print & Dispatch
expectedPersonas.shape: Full control of Print Jobs and Dispatches; read-only on the application except its Status. Gains Edit on the application at Printing/Dispatch/Delivered via Fulfilment Stage To Fulfilment.

expectedPersonas.label: Passport Office Manager / RPO
expectedPersonas.shape: Read/edit everything in the office, plus Risk Flags and blacklisted citizens via the manager sharing rules. Also the approver-to-be once an approval process exists (P0-02).

expectedPersonas.label: Audit & Compliance
expectedPersonas.shape: Read-only across every PSK object including Notification Logs and field history. No create, edit or delete anywhere — this is the set to test hardest, because a stray allowEdit in it is invisible until an auditor changes something.

expectedPersonas.label: Reference Data Admin
expectedPersonas.shape: Maintains the reference layer — PSK__c offices and Slot__c capacity — without any access to applicant personal data. The one persona that should fail a read on Citizen__c.

personaMatrix.personaGroups: Three permission set groups bundle these for staff who wear two hats: PSK_Front_Office (Officer + Verification Officer), PSK_Back_Office (Granting + Fulfilment) and PSK_Leadership (Office Manager + Auditor). Groups must contain only references to the persona sets — never permissions of their own.
personaMatrix.personaCaveat: The seven persona sets landed during this audit. The matrix above is rendered from whatever PSK_* permission sets are on disk at generation time — including PSK_App_Access, which is the admin catch-all and is expected to be wide. The row shapes below are the design intent; where the matrix disagrees with the intent, the metadata is what shipped and needs a decision.

actionItems.item: Hardcoded OpenAI API key. classes/OpenAIChatController.cls is documented in CLAUDE.md as containing a hardcoded OpenAI API key in source. The file is no longer present in the repository and does not appear anywhere in git history — it was removed (or never committed) before this audit. The key must still be treated as compromised: rotate it at the provider, and if the class is ever reinstated, move the secret to a Named Credential or protected Custom Metadata. Also remove the stale warning from CLAUDE.md so it stops sending readers after a file that is not there.

No Approval Process exists anywhere in the org. force-app/main/default/approvalProcesses/ is absent entirely. Granting a Diplomatic or Official passport — the highest-consequence action in the system — is today a picklist change by any user with edit access on the record. Build at least one: Diplomatic/Official Grant Approval, entry criteria Passport_Category__c IN (Diplomatic, Official) AND Status__c = Granting, approver the Regional Passport Officer role, with field updates locking the record on approval. A second process for high-risk grants (Risk_Score__c > 70) is the obvious follow-up.

Enterprise Territory Management is not enabled and cannot be enabled by deploy. Confirmed by query: SELECT Id FROM Territory2Model fails with "sObject type 'Territory2Model' is not supported". ETM is a Setup toggle (Setup → Territory Settings → Enable Enterprise Territory Management) and is irreversible once on; no metadata deployment can flip it. Until someone makes that call, region-based access must be built from public groups plus criteria-based sharing rules — which is what the org does today. Decide explicitly whether to enable it or to commit to the group-based approach, and write the decision down.

Region-based sharing needs a real text field on the application. Criteria-based sharing rules cannot traverse a lookup and cannot read a formula field, so no rule can be written against PSK_Office__r.Region__c. The Passport__c sharing rule already carries a comment acknowledging the same limitation for its formula fields. Add a plain Region__c Text or Picklist field to Passport_Application__c, populate it from PSK_Office__r.Region__c in the before-save trigger (and backfill existing rows), then write one criteria-based rule per region sharing to the matching public group.
actionItems.verify: generator: presence of Region__c on Passport_Application__c

actionItems.item: Per-record-type Lightning record page activation is a manual step. Org-default and app-default page assignments deploy fine, but per-record-type activation is not reliably representable in FlexiPage metadata and must be done in Lightning App Builder. After every deploy that touches record pages, open each page → Activation → App, Record Type and Profile, and assign it. Pages needing activation are listed in the table below this section (enumerated from flexipages/ at generation time). At minimum: Passport_Application_Record_Page against all six application record types in the Application Management Console, and App_Home as that app's home page.

No reports, dashboards or custom report types exist for any PSK object. reportTypes/ contains only inherited template types (flow orchestration, partner fund, MDF) and there is no reports/ or dashboards/ directory at all. Nothing in the org can answer an operational question in aggregate. Build custom report types for Application-with-Payments, Application-with-Police-Verification and Passport-with-Dispatch, then a manager dashboard: applications by stage, ageing against SLA_Config__mdt, Tatkal SLA breach count, PV turnaround, print/dispatch throughput.
actionItems.verify: generator: reports/ and dashboards/ directory presence; PSK-named reportTypes

actionItems.item: No Experience Cloud citizen self-service site. The applicant journey is entirely staff-mediated: a citizen cannot start a draft, upload a document, pay a fee or check status without an officer doing it for them. The org does contain an inherited Internal Zone community and the standard self-registration controllers, but those are Service Analytics template leftovers, not a PSK portal — do not mistake them for progress. Building this is the largest single remaining piece of scope.

Citizen_Required_On_Submit ships inactive on purpose and must be activated only after the citizen backfill has run. Activating it before every existing application has a Citizen__c value will make historical records unsaveable — any later edit to an old application would be blocked by a rule about a field that was optional when it was created. Sequence: backfill Citizen__c on all applications, verify zero nulls, then flip <active> to true and deploy the single rule. The generator reports the rule's live state in the validation-rule appendix; if it is absent from the appendix, it has not been written yet.
actionItems.verify: generator: Citizen_Required_On_Submit validation rule presence + active flag

actionItems.item: Several PSK objects have no page layout in the tree. layouts/ contains layouts for the older objects but none for Citizen__c, Passport__c, Print_Job__c, Dispatch__c or Family_Member__c, which are the newest additions. They will fall back to an auto-generated layout, which puts fields in an arbitrary order and gives testers nothing to check against. Author a layout per object with the same section ordering convention as the application layout. (The generator lists which objects are missing a layout as of generation.)
actionItems.verify: generator: layouts/ cross-referenced against object list

actionItems.item: The Path covers only the Fresh record type. pathAssistants/Passport_Application_Path declares <recordTypeName>Fresh</recordTypeName>, so the other five record types — Re-issue, Tatkal, Lost/Damaged, Minor, Diplomatic/Official — render no stage bar at all. Either add a path assistant per record type (they can share guidance text) or document that the Path is Fresh-only by design.
actionItems.verify: generator: pathAssistants inventory and record types covered

actionItems.item: Shield Platform Encryption is unavailable in Developer Edition, so Aadhaar_Token__c is plain text. This is a platform-edition constraint, not a defect to fix here — but it makes the discipline load-bearing: never populate Aadhaar_Token__c with an Aadhaar number, a hash of one, or anything else that could re-identify a person. It exists to hold an opaque provider reference. The DPDP-driven rule stands: store Aadhaar_Verified__c as the fact and the token as the receipt, never the number. Restrict the field to the manager and auditor personas via FLS, and add a note on the field description saying so.
actionItems.verify: generator: Aadhaar_Token__c field type + encryption scheme

actionItems.item: Stray metadata to clean up, with the owner's consent before any delete. classes/ABC.cls (21 bytes) and classes/TestSheet.cls (27 bytes) are empty stubs. classes/LeadController.cls is unrelated to PSK. layouts/Lead-Passport Application %28New%29 Layout.layout-meta.xml is an orphan Lead page layout named after this project — confusing precisely because the name looks relevant. And contentassets/ holds a large number of near-duplicate _1/_11 variants of the same images. None of this breaks anything; all of it costs a reader time. (The generator reports the live counts.)
actionItems.verify: generator: file sizes and contentassets duplicate count

actionItems.item: objectTranslations/ are empty en_US stubs. Every bundle is <Object>-en_US restating the English label — there is no Hindi and no regional translation, despite Citizen__c.Preferred_Language__c existing to record what language a citizen wants to be dealt with in. A passport office that records a language preference and then cannot honour it is worse than one that does not ask. Either add a real hi translation for the applicant-facing labels and picklist values, or drop Preferred_Language__c until the capability exists.

manifest/package.xml is a wildcard manifest covering nearly 200 metadata types. Every retrieve pulls the whole org, including the Service Analytics / Wave template noise, which is slow and buries PSK changes in unrelated diffs. Add a second, scoped manifest/psk-package.xml listing only the PSK objects, layouts, permission sets, groups, queues, roles, sharing rules, custom metadata, global value sets, flexipages, LWCs, tabs, apps, path assistants and PSK_* Apex, and use it as the day-to-day retrieve target. Keep the full manifest for disaster recovery.
actionItems.verify: generator: count of <name> entries in manifest/package.xml

actionItems.item: Apex apiVersion drift. The older PSK_* classes and their tests carry apiVersion 61.0 in their .cls-meta.xml while sfdx-project.json sets sourceApiVersion 67.0. Nothing is broken, but the mismatch means new classes and old classes can behave differently on version-gated platform behaviour. Bump the PSK classes to 67.0 and re-run the test suite in one deliberate change rather than discovering it during a future upgrade.
actionItems.verify: generator: apiVersion values across PSK_* cls-meta.xml

storageIntro: Developer Edition gives roughly 5 MB of data storage. Salesforce bills most records at 2 KB each regardless of how many fields are populated, which puts the practical ceiling at about 2,500 records org-wide — not per object.

That ceiling is already substantially consumed by metadata inherited with the Service Analytics / CRM Analytics template, which was retrieved into this org before PSK work began. The record-count chart in this section shows where the space has gone.

This is why the demo-data generator targets roughly 1,200–1,500 records at scale 1. It is not a modesty figure — it is what is left. A generator that produced a "realistic" 10,000 applications would fail partway through with a storage error and leave the org in a half-seeded state that is harder to reason about than an empty one.

deleteFirst.why: The single largest block, and entirely template sample activity data. Nothing in PSK reads it. Deleting these frees more room than everything else combined.
Service Analytics sample cases. PSK does not use Case at all.
Wave dashboard feed data. Deleting it breaks the inherited Service Analytics dashboards — acceptable, since they are not part of PSK. Delete OpportunityHistory__c first to avoid orphan rows.

The application's legacy Applicant__c lookup points at Account, so check nothing PSK-owned references an Account before deleting. Citizen__c is the intended identity object; Account is only still there for the earlier design.
Small, but free to remove — none are referenced by PSK metadata.
Deleted records keep consuming storage until the Recycle Bin is purged. sf data delete bulk plus Empty Recycle Bin, or storage will not appear to move at all.

licenceNote: The org has 3 Salesforce licences, all 3 in use, and 3 Salesforce Platform licences with 1 in use — 2 free. There is no room to stand up one user per persona.

Persona testing therefore uses a single Salesforce Platform user with permission sets swapped between passes, rather than six or seven dedicated users. Assign one PSK_* set, run that persona's rows in the access matrix, remove the set, assign the next.

Two consequences to be honest about. First, a swapped-set user does not prove that concurrent personas see the right things — anything that depends on record ownership by a different user (queue assignment, the owner-based half of the role hierarchy) needs a second real user, and there are two Platform licences available for exactly that.

Second, the Salesforce Platform licence itself withholds some objects and features that a full Salesforce licence grants. Do not read a Platform-user access failure as a permission-set bug until the licence has been ruled out.

appendix.commandsIntro: Run from the repository root. psk-dev is the project's default target-org, so --target-org is optional throughout.

commandGroups.title: 1. Validate before you touch the org

commands.note: Full validation, nothing saved. Always do this first.
Narrower and much faster while iterating on the data model.
Value sets first — picklist fields reference them.
Objects, fields, record types, validation rules, compact layouts, list views.

commands.cmd: sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app/main/default/layouts --source-dir force-app/main/default/flexipages
commands.note: Layouts and Lightning pages, once the fields they reference exist.
Roles before groups — groups reference roles.

commands.cmd: sf project deploy start --metadata Group --metadata Queue
commands.note: Public groups and work queues.

commands.cmd: sf project deploy start --metadata PermissionSet --metadata PermissionSetGroup
commands.note: Personas. Field-level security lives here.
Sharing rules last — they reference groups, roles and fields.
Fee_Matrix__mdt and SLA_Config__mdt records.

commands.cmd: sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app/main/default/lwc --source-dir force-app/main/default/classes
commands.note: Apex and LWC.

commands.cmd: sf project deploy start --metadata CustomApplication --metadata CustomTab --metadata PathAssistant
commands.note: App shell, tabs and the Path.

commands.cmd: sf apex run test --test-level RunLocalTests --result-format human --code-coverage
commands.note: Whole local suite with coverage.

commands.cmd: sf apex run test --class-names PSK_HomeControllerTest --result-format human
commands.note: A single class while iterating.

commands.cmd: sf data query -q "SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM Passport_Application__c"
commands.note: Confirm rows are visible to the running user.
Open the app and eyeball the home page and tab set.
Lightning App Builder — do the manual per-record-type page activations (P1-03).

commands.cmd: sf data query -q "SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM Passport_Application__c"
commands.note: Baseline count before seeding, so the delta is provable.
Anonymous-Apex seed at scale 1 (~1,200–1,500 records). Check the exact script name in scripts/apex/.
Watch it run; a storage failure shows up here, not in the CLI exit code.
Storage usage page — confirm you have not hit the 5 MB ceiling.
Full-org retrieve. Slow — nearly 200 wildcard types (see P2-04).
One object, which is what you usually want.
